text:
Aliaksei Protas scored 25 goals last season and has 2 this year, and the gap between those numbers is mostly bad luck. Through 22 games he has 5.5 expected goals (the quality of his chances), shooting 5% against a usual range around 13%. He's gone seven games without a goal on 2.7 expected. The looks are there; the puck isn't going in.

The rest of his game says the same. Washington gets 56.3% of the expected goals with the 6'6" Belarusian on the ice at five on five, 4.1 points better than without him, and he has 10 assists, 7 in the last ten games alone. Evolving-Hockey had him 92nd percentile among forwards at driving offense last season, though with a cost at the other end, where opponents also got more with him out there.

One oddity: he has no power-play points this season. The Capitals have lost seven of their last ten, and they need the version of Protas who finishes. Our range for his season sits at 12 to 24 goals, which tells you how much of this is expected to come back.
